headline: Second check of the client bundles: all 13 findings are real on a re-measure of the built chunks (5 confirmed, 8 corrected in scope, numbers or fix, none refuted), and none rests on a feature being unused: every cost here is bytes each owner or shopper will download and parse on a page load once the platform opens, and before opening is the cheapest time to cut them. Shoppers' pages are lean: a store page's first scripts are 664 to 760 KB raw (239 to 278 KB gzip) and about 480 KB of that is React and Next. The admin is where the weight is: 432 signed-in routes carry the Supabase client (253 KB) and zod (114 KB) first; three small import changes plus lazy upload helpers take about 495 KB off 266 routes, 350 to 400 KB off 126 and 253 KB off the 39 builder routes. The rich text editor (435 KB) is in 73 routes' first scripts, and nine page lists carry it only because their server module also imports the categories view. The builder ships four storefront languages whole (311 KB). One Work screen loads 4.27 MB. Kaizena Flow's front page prefetches the admin (437 KB) for a link that is a full page load anyway. Main corrections: the session cut alone covers 349 routes, not 432; zod stays on about 160 routes; the cookie table is also read by the consent manager; the browser's CSS coverage undercounts (a store page names about 10% of the utility rules); the duplicate-module figure (6.89 of 17.1 MB) is deploy size and costs a browser about 14% while moving around; loaded.json's module lists are wrong, as the auditor said.

metrics.name: Units and method of this second check
metrics.value: KB is 1,024 bytes unless a figure is given in bytes. Every chunk in .next/static/chunks (530 files, 17,978,154 bytes) was split into its Turbopack modules with my own parser; an import graph was built from each module's e.i()/e.r() calls; each route's client roots came from its page_client-reference-manifest.js; a cut is simulated by removing an edge and summing what is no longer reachable. The model gives 1,137 KB for the admin home against 1,167 KB in the build's stats.

metrics.value: Confirmed: its module lists are wrong, its totals right. loaded.md gives the store home 28 KB of moving.en.ts in 01fvsecug_p8v.js, but 'Bring your Shopify shop' is only in 2ps0djrg5x1ff.js and 2m8xr7ciiqquz.js, which no store page loads; it gives 33fehdj3n8030.js (Next's layout-router chunk, in every route) to the inline CSS editor. Real figures: store home 6 KB of admin text (common.en) and no inline editor; admin home about 92 KB of catalogues in scripts (builder.en 70, home.en 22) plus the small ones kept at hand. So the brief's 'facts already seen' of 35 KB, 9 KB and 299 KB do not stand.
metrics.how: rg of distinctive strings over .next/static/chunks; cats.mjs

clean: No route outside /admin carries zod, the Supabase client, a whole storefront language or an admin text catalogue over 10 KB in its first scripts: checked on all 111 such routes (the auditor wrote 130) and their 63 chunk files. The rule in docs/performance.md and storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts holds.

No storefront route loads a whole language (D212 holds): the chunk with all four (1u2592k6jkhim.js) is listed by 40 admin routes only. The small browser-text modules load with every page by a written rule (a press before a lazily loaded language arrived was lost, docs/performance.md), so they are left alone.

The heavy optional parts stay out until drawn: three and model-viewer are one 1.08 MB chunk no measured page loaded (the product page's gallery only names the element); no measured store page loaded CodeMirror, Stripe's SDK, the lightbox or tiptap.

The owner's inline editors on the storefront load only when the mode is turned on (page-edit-link.tsx:12-14, next/dynamic with ssr off). The string kaizen_site_css_panel in a store page's scripts comes from the cookie table, not from the editor.
The admin's English is lazy per area as D540 says: admin-text-later.ts has 54 import() calls, and the AI manager's chat is fetched on opening (ai-manager-launcher.tsx:32).
The docs page (485 KB, about 465 of it framework) and the admin's sign-in (482 KB) are close to the framework floor.
Icons are per-icon modules: about 40 KB on an admin screen, none in a store home's first-load chunks by the same count.

Scripts and styles are served with public, max-age=31536000, immutable (routes.json), so a returning person pays the download again only for chunk files a deploy changed; what repeats on each full page load is parsing and running.

The cart, checkout, order and account forms in their own routes' first scripts are there by a tested rule (docs/performance.md: what is pressed before a part's script runs is lost): not bloat on those routes.

The list of every store's hosts does not reach the browser: no client chunk of this build contains the JSON.parse of NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_HOSTS, though paths.ts is imported by client code (the function is shaken out).

The storefront chunks an admin screen fetched after load here (206 KB) come from prefetching the View store link under /s/{store}; storeHref() makes that link cross-origin in production (paths.ts:207), so it is not prefetched there.
Class names written only in test files add 0.4 KB to the shared stylesheet, and none comes only from the migrations' SQL: the @source lines in globals.css cost nothing worth cutting.
No finding of this dimension argues from a feature being unused or a table being empty; nothing here proposes retiring, hiding or merging a feature.

findings.title: Every signed-in admin screen loads the whole Supabase client in its first scripts, for a listener that refreshes the session
findings.evidence: Chunks 2du16ociar189.js (179,419 bytes, 44.6 KB gzip: one merged module of supabase-js, auth-js, storage, postgrest, @supabase/ssr and env.ts) and 2i4juo9spco86.js (57,349 bytes, realtime and phoenix) are in the first-load list of 432 of 560 routes; on the admin home 13% and 12% of them ran. The Supabase module also brings Next's buffer polyfill (22 KB). In the built import graph, on the home, orders, settings and platform home the only importer is session.tsx (module 483633), whose SessionKeeper calls createClient().auth.onAuthStateChange(() => {}) in an effect. Removing that edge takes 253 KB off those screens. Over all 432 routes the session edge alone removes Supabase on 349; on 83 it stays through static imports in nine upload and import files (the auditor listed five). The server does not refresh the session: proxy.ts has no Supabase call.
findings.cost: 253 KB raw (about 68 KB gzip, 72 as transferred) in the first scripts of 432 routes; 87% of it does not run there. The files are immutable, so the download is once per browser until they change; the parse and start-up run on every full page load.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on each admin screen (today the team; every owner once the platform opens), and a visitor of Kaizena Flow's front page through BN-2.
findings.fix: Load the client where it is used: in session.tsx, await import("@/lib/supabase/client") inside the effect, and the same in the nine upload and import files, which all call it inside async handlers. Split the two public variables out of env.ts without zod first, or the lazy group drags zod (114 KB) along. To remove bytes for good, a second step: keep the session with @supabase/auth-js alone (drops realtime, storage, postgrest, functions and the polyfill, about 126 KB, estimate), or refresh the cookie on the server (the comment at lib/supabase/server.ts:27 says that was the plan), which costs the server an occasional call to Supabase Auth on admin requests.
findings.saving: Simulated on the real chunks: 253 KB off the first scripts; 349 routes with session.tsx alone, all 432 with the nine other files (admin home 1,137 to 884 KB from this cut). After step one the same bytes still load after hydration on every full page load; only step two removes them (about half, estimate). No time was measured.
findings.risk: Low. The keeper starts one request later than today. A first upload waits for a chunk. The signed-in end-to-end suite covers sign-in and uploads.
findings.already_tracked: PERF-01 in docs/audits/psi-followups.md (line 482) is open and says to cut the shared scripts; it does not name this cut.
findings.verify_note: Re-opened the layout, session.tsx, the client and all importers (rg found ten, the auditor cited six). Re-measured chunk sizes, coverage, the 432-route count and the 253 KB cut with my own split of the built chunks. Changed: the session change alone covers 349 routes, not 432; nine helper files, not five; 'on every admin screen' is a download once per browser and a parse per full load; env.ts must be split or zod follows the lazy client. Does not rest on anything being unused.

findings.title: Kaizena Flow's front page prefetches the admin and downloads its signed-in frame
findings.evidence: The front page's HTML asks for 650 KB of scripts, as a store's home does (664). After load the router prefetches /admin (the Sign in links are plain next/link) and the browser fetches the six scripts of the gated layout's entry list: 2du16ociar189 (179,419 bytes), 1-5xy7dnrat0_ (116,870), 2i4juo9spco86 (57,349), 2zizbcwzl-te- (50,434), 0hqyp5k5log8u (18,934), 3fkl-rwp5s-t7 (14,433), and the admin's stylesheet (21,083). Coverage: 95 to 580 bytes of each ran. That is 437,439 bytes, more than the 411 KB by which this page's loaded scripts exceed a store home's (1,150 against 739 KB). Two things make it pure waste: / and /admin have different root layouts, and Next's docs say a move across root layouts is a full page load, so the prefetched payload is thrown away; and a visitor who is not signed in lands on /admin/sign-in, whose own first scripts hold none of the five large files. Only four links in src set prefetch={false}. The sign-in page does the same toward the site (242 KB after load).
findings.cost: 437 KB raw / 135 KB transferred of scripts and a 6 KB (gzip) stylesheet per first visit to the front page, on top of the 230 KB gzip the page needs: 59% more script bytes.
findings.who_pays: Every first-time visitor of kaizenaflow.com. Few today; this grows with marketing traffic the day the platform opens.
findings.fix: prefetch={false} on the links from the public site to /admin, and on the sign-in page's links back to the site. BN-1 and BN-4 also shrink what any such prefetch pulls, since the six files are the gated layout's entry list.
findings.saving: Measured: 437,439 bytes raw / 134,674 transferred of scripts and the 21 KB stylesheet per first visit; the page's script transfer falls from about 400 to about 269 KB.
findings.risk: Low. The press on Sign in is a full page load either way, so nothing a person sees gets slower. Measured on the local production build; the links are relative, so production behaves the same.
findings.verify_note: Re-opened the five links and listed routes.json's responses in order: the /admin prefetch, then the six scripts, each in /admin's first-load list and not in /'s. Sizes and transfer re-added (437,439 / 134,674). Read Next's link and layout docs: prefetch={false} never prefetches, and crossing root layouts reloads the page, which the auditor did not say and which strengthens the case. Not about an unused feature.

findings.title: The keyboard shortcut sheet brings the page builder's words and field code to every admin screen
findings.evidence: shortcut-sheet.tsx, drawn by the admin's frame, imports one four-line function (typingIn) from responsive-edit.tsx. That module imports builderEn by value (the builder's whole English, used as a default argument at line 100), DisplayFields and lib/responsive. In the built chunks the chain is module 562883 (shortcut sheet, 2.3 KB) to 998934 (responsive-edit with display fields, 24.3 KB) to 22118 (builderEn, 69.7 KB), and on the admin home it is the only chain to them. 0pmozty218j-z.js (71,508 bytes) is in the first-load list of 423 routes; the browser marks it 100% run because it is one object literal, but no list screen reads it.
findings.cost: 129 KB raw (about 43 KB gzip for the three chunks) in the first scripts of 335 routes, 96 to 111 KB on 48 more; nothing on the 39 builder routes, which need these modules.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on every admin screen that is not the builder.
findings.fix: Move typingIn (and isResponsiveShortcut) to a small module of their own, say src/lib/typing-in.ts, and import it from there. In responsive-edit.tsx make words a required argument and keep only import type of the catalogue.
findings.saving: Simulated on the real chunks: 129 KB off 335 routes' first scripts, 96 to 111 KB off 48, 58 KB off one, none off the 39 builder routes (the auditor said 129 KB off all 423).
findings.risk: None seen: no behaviour changes. responsive-edit.tsx then leaves the scan test's list, which that test requires.
findings.already_tracked: Partly: responsive-edit.tsx is on the list in admin-catalogues.scan.test.ts that may only shrink; that the admin's frame imports it is not noted anywhere. PERF-01 (open) covers the shared scripts in general.
findings.verify_note: Re-opened all cited lines. Traced the chain in the built chunks (chain.mjs) and simulated the cut on every route with builderEn first (bn3.mjs). The mechanism and the 129 KB hold; the scope is 335 routes in full and 48 in part, not 423. Not about an unused feature.

findings.title: zod is in every signed-in admin screen's first scripts through three small imports
findings.evidence: Chunk 1-5xy7dnrat0_.js is zod (116,870 bytes, 33.0 KB gzip) in the first-load list of 432 routes; 27% of it ran on the admin home (schemas built at import). On the admin home its importers are: the Supabase module, where env.ts is merged and publicEnv() checks two strings; push-settings.tsx, which takes deviceName from push.ts, a module that also holds a zod schema, while the layout only wants AdminServiceWorker from it; and typography, visibility and colour through BN-3's chain. After BN-1 and BN-3 the only importer left there is push-settings.tsx.
findings.cost: 114 KB raw, 33 to 35 KB gzip, in the first scripts of 432 routes.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on each admin screen.
findings.fix: Give the admin's frame the storefront's rule: schemas live in *-schema.ts beside the plain module. Move pushSubscriptionInput to push-schema.ts; check the two public variables in env.ts by hand, or split a public-env.ts without zod. Add the frame's client roots to a scan that walks imports, as storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts does.
findings.saving: Simulated on the real chunks: zod leaves the first scripts of 260 routes with BN-1's session change and BN-3, and of 275 once every Supabase importer is lazy; it stays on about 160 routes whose own code imports it (the page model, custom fields, the builder). On the list screens the three findings together take 495 KB off (admin home 1,137 to 642 KB, 44%).
findings.risk: Low. The server still validates the push subscription with the schema.
findings.already_tracked: The rule exists for visitors only (docs/performance.md, No zod in a visitor's scripts); PERF-01 is open in general.
findings.verify_note: Re-opened env.ts, push.ts, push-settings.tsx and the layout. Listed zod's importers in the admin home's chunks before and after the two other cuts (zod.mjs): only push-settings.tsx is left, as the auditor said. Changed: zod does not leave all 432 routes; it leaves 260 to 275, and the routes that keep it are not only editors but also lists and detail pages with custom fields.

findings.title: The rich text editor is in the first scripts of 73 routes; nine page lists carry it only because their server module also holds the categories view
findings.evidence: Chunk 3lclkawi229rq.js (tiptap and prosemirror, 435,421 bytes, 136,630 gzip) is in the first-load list of 73 routes: 39 of the builder family and 34 others. The 34 are nine lists of pages, articles, headers, footers and product layouts (1.96 MB each), five category pages, twelve content type screens, three custom field screens, the order, customer and deal pages and the product editor twice. On the pages list 0% of the chunk ran, on the product editor 6%. Two importers of the editor in the built chunks: fields-form (custom fields of the rich text kind, reached on the order page through EntityFieldsCard) and the terms manager with a term's own page (which also brings @dnd-kit, 42 KB). The nine lists reach the terms manager only because views.tsx, their server module, imports TermsManager for the categories view at line 247: a route loads every client component its server module imports (docs/performance.md).
findings.cost: 439 KB raw (about 137 KB gzip) for the editor alone on 34 routes that draw no rich text at first paint, 654 KB on each of the nine lists with the terms manager, drag and drop and the custom fields form.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on lists, orders, customers, deals and the product editor: the screens an owner with a real shop opens most.
findings.fix: Two parts. (1) Move the categories view out of the lists' views.tsx into its own server module, as editor-views.tsx was split out on 4 November: no lazy loading, so no early press can be lost. Check the content lists' module for the same shape. (2) Where the editor may be drawn (the order, customer and deal pages, the product editor, the category pages, content entries), one next/dynamic stand-in for RichTextEditor used by fields-form.tsx and term-page-fields.tsx, showing the saved text until the script arrives.
findings.saving: Simulated on the real chunks: part 1 takes 654 KB off each of the nine lists (1,922 to 1,269 KB; to 919 with BN-1, BN-3 and BN-4). Part 2 takes 439 KB off the order page, the customer page and the product editor (order page 1,918 to 1,130 and product editor 2,047 to 1,259 with the frame cuts).
findings.risk: Part 1 low. Part 2 medium: docs/performance.md records that a part waiting for its script loses an early press, so the stand-in must not accept typing before the editor is there, and the signed-in tests for content types and products must pass.
findings.already_tracked: Code review step 3.4 (FB8, Open) covers the builder's own dialogs and editor. The lists, the order, customer and deal pages and the product editor are not named; docs/performance.md describes the 4 November split that left the categories view in views.tsx.
findings.verify_note: Recounted the 73 routes (39 builder, 34 others) and re-read coverage. Traced the importers in the built chunks and simulated both cuts. Changed: the 34 are not all 'not editors' (the product editor and four content entry screens can draw rich text); the nine lists have a cheaper and safer fix the auditor missed, which also saves more (654 against 503 KB); the editor-only saving is 439 KB. The auditor's line product-editor.tsx:32 is the TermPicker import, which is the right chain.

findings.title: The page builder ships all four storefront languages whole
findings.evidence: Chunk 1u2592k6jkhim.js (318,693 bytes, 103,098 gzip) is one merged module of lib/i18n with lib/messages sv, nb, da and en (311 KB), in the first-load list of 40 routes: the 39 of the builder family and the draft order editor. Five built modules import it: the builder, block-fields, modal-preview, a grid part and the draft order editor. Each reads a few keys through t(lang) in one language at a time (a form's usual words, a modal's, a grid's). A second module (32 KB) holds the four returns texts and leaves with it.
findings.cost: 343 KB raw (about 110 KB gzip) on each builder load, of which one language (about 68 KB) can be read at a time.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser each time a page, header, footer, article or layout is opened in the builder.
findings.fix: Have the builder's server page hand down the texts its previews read, in the languages the store has, as it already hands down the admin's areas; or import one language on demand when the edited language changes. Then lib/i18n leaves the builder's client graph and a scan can hold it out, as storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts does for visitors. The draft order editor needs the same.
findings.saving: Simulated on the real chunks: 343 KB off the builder's first scripts if the texts are handed down (3,186 to 2,591 KB together with BN-1); 368 KB off the draft order editor. About 235 KB if one language stays as a script (estimate). Texts handed down move into the document, which is not cached, so hand down only the keys read.
findings.risk: Medium. Previews of store parts inside the builder must still find every key they draw, in each language of the store and in a language translated by AI (ui-registry); a missing one shows English.
findings.already_tracked: Not as a step. docs/performance.md (D212) states that the admin reads all four languages through t(); code review step 3.4 (Open) is about the builder's dialogs, not this.
findings.verify_note: Re-opened i18n.ts and the four import sites; listed the chunk's modules (one of 311 KB) and its importers in the built graph; simulated the cut (343 KB, the auditor 342). Added: a store with several languages needs each one handed down or fetched, not one. Not about an unused feature.

findings.title: One Work screen loads 4.27 MB: the admin's whole text in both languages
findings.evidence: /admin/account/work/s/[store]/invoices/[invoiceId] has 4,274,839 bytes of first scripts in the build's stats, the largest of 560 routes; the invoices list beside it has 1,262,262. Its 16 extra chunk files are 3,016,959 bytes: 3fqt1dd2f0p1k.js (1,704,595 bytes, 526 KB gzip, in no other route), whose one 1.64 MB module is the draft editor merged with lib/admin-text.ts and every Norwegian catalogue ('Lagre' 548 times), and twelve files with 46 English catalogues (1,216,985 bytes). ReadinessList and InvoiceTotalsView have no use client and read their words through lib/work-text.ts, which imports lib/admin-text.ts (135 imports: every area in two languages); two client components import them, so all of it becomes browser code. Of the 47 importers of work-text.ts, only these two are reachable from a client component. work-text.ts keeps the language in React's cache(), which does not memoise outside server components, so in the browser these two parts read English (by reading the code; not run).
findings.cost: 2.9 MB raw more than its sibling screens on each first open of a Work invoice draft; the 1.7 MB chunk alone is 526 KB gzip.
findings.who_pays: An owner or accountant using Work's invoices; the build too, which compiles the catalogues a second time for the client.
findings.fix: Pass the words to ReadinessList and InvoiceTotalsView as props from the server page, as other admin parts do, so no client module imports work-text.ts. Add lib/admin-text.ts and lib/work-text.ts to a scan that fails when a client module reaches them.
findings.saving: About 2.9 MB raw on that route, to about 1.3 MB, the level of its sibling screens (estimate from the route's extra chunks).
findings.risk: Low. It also corrects the language those two parts show to a Norwegian account.
findings.verify_note: Re-opened the five files and admin-text.ts. Recomputed the route's extra chunks against its sibling (3,016,959 bytes), found the Norwegian catalogues inside the 1.7 MB chunk and 46 English ones in twelve files, and walked imports from every client component to confirm that only two files bring work-text.ts in. The English-in-the-browser point is from reading the code. Not about an unused feature: the cost is per open of that screen.

findings.title: Whole English catalogues are imported as default values, and the check sees only the direct ones
findings.evidence: Many modules import an area's whole English catalogue as a value, nearly always for a default argument (words = builderEn, c = commonEn.features). The scan test looks only at files that start with use client and import a catalogue directly (line 48), and lists 14. A walk of value imports from all 495 client components finds 14 such client files and about 25 plain modules they reach (field-group-editor, redirect-admin, templates-helpers, store-features, analytics-words, return-admin, shipping-method-form, tax-profile, work-ui and others) that the test cannot see; the auditor counted 21 with the bundler's graph. In the build's first-load lists: 84 KB of catalogues on average over the 432 signed-in routes; the builder family 146 KB (builder 70, blocks 53, fields 23); the AI manager's page 167; the product editor 112 (builder 70, fields 23, redirects 19); the admin home 92 (builder 70, home 22); orders 84 (builder 70, orders 14). On the builder page 'Separator line' is in the document four times and in a script too: an English reader gets the words twice, and a Norwegian reader downloads English never shown.
findings.cost: 14 to 97 KB raw per admin screen beyond BN-3's 70 KB; 319 KB of second copies of blocks.en alone across chunk files.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on the builder, the product editor, orders, the home and the AI manager's page.
findings.fix: Make the words a required argument in modules a client can reach and keep import type of the catalogue; where a default is wanted for tests or server code, put it in a server-only wrapper. Replace the test's file filter with a walk of imports from every client root, as storefront-bundle.scan.test.ts does, so plain modules count.
findings.saving: Estimate from module sizes: builder minus 76 KB beyond BN-3's 70; product editor minus 42; admin home minus 22; orders minus 14; the AI manager's page minus 97.
findings.risk: Medium: many call sites and tests lean on the defaults; the type checker finds them all.
findings.already_tracked: Partly: PERF-01 and D540 removed the fallback, and the test's list of 14 may only shrink; the plain modules and the default-argument pattern are not tracked.
findings.verify_note: Re-read the scan test and seven of the cited imports. Measured catalogue bytes per route in the built chunks (cats.mjs): mean 84 KB (the auditor 82), builder 146, AI manager 167, home 92. My source walk gives 14 client files and about 25 plain modules against the auditor's 15 and 21: the same picture. Checked the 'twice' claim in the saved HTML of the builder and the product editor.

findings.title: Listing and other built pages carry the cart's, checkout's, order's and account's forms
findings.evidence: 15 storefront routes have 715 to 768 KB of first scripts against 668 to 680 for 42 others. Category, tag, search, wishlist, cookies and deliveries are among them. RolePage hands every such route one drawer, StorePartSection, which imports each working page's section; the function returns null unless the part belongs to the route (drawsOn). So a category page has 19 client roots a store's home does not: account sign-in, checkout button, delivery choice, quote request, the consent manager, gift and discount forms, booking changes. Its four extra chunk files are 102,465 bytes (32.0 KB gzip). On the empty cart three of these chunks (98 KB) ran 0 to 1%.
findings.cost: 96 KB raw, 30 KB gzip, more than a store's home on each first view of a category, tag, search or wishlist page; less on the cart and checkout, which need their own share.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser on listing pages, on the first visit to each store (each store's host has its own cache).
findings.fix: The next step of D461: each route passes a drawer that imports only its own parts (a listing's, the cart's, the checkout's), sharing one small switch. drawsOn() already says which part belongs where.
findings.saving: Simulated on the category route by dropping the roots it cannot draw: 73 KB (the auditor, keeping some) to 94 KB (all 19) raw, up to 30 KB gzip.
findings.risk: Medium. The forms that the rule in docs/performance.md keeps in the first scripts must stay on their own routes; the end-to-end tests named there guard that.
findings.already_tracked: Partly: docs/performance.md (D461) did this split once, at the level of RolePage; the split per route is not planned.
findings.verify_note: Re-opened RolePage, StorePartSection, the listing route and drawsOn. Recounted the route sizes (15 high, 42 at 668 to 680, one at 484). Compared the category route's client roots with the home's (19 extra) and measured its extra chunks (102,465 bytes, 31,956 gzip); my simulation gives 94 KB where the auditor's gave 73. 'Most visited kind' is a fair guess, not a measurement: there are no shoppers yet.

findings.title: Three tables a shopper's page never reads at first paint are in its first scripts
findings.evidence: (1) cookie-consent.ts is one built module of 24,640 bytes, and 23,860 of them (97%; 6.4 KB gzip) are KNOWN_COOKIES: 38 cookies, each with its purpose in four languages (18,702 bytes of purposes). page-modal.ts and ab-assign.tsx take three small exports from it; its chunk ran 6% on the store home. The table is in six chunk files. One client reader the auditor missed: the consent manager's forget() tests each cookie's name against the table's patterns and categories (consent-manager.tsx:230); it is loaded only where a banner is drawn (lazy/extras.tsx). (2) The header's Private or Business switch imports cookie helpers from b2b.ts, which imports the feature registry (5.5 KB), which imports the admin's common English (6.1 KB) for default labels. (3) theme-preview-stage.tsx (4.8 KB), the theme store's stage, is a client root of every store page because the page renderer imports the theme store's parts.
findings.cost: About 40 KB raw (about 12 KB gzip, estimate) of the 189 KB that is the app's share of a store home's first scripts; on every storefront and site page.
findings.who_pays: Every shopper's browser, on the first page of each store they visit.
findings.fix: Split the cookie table: names, patterns and categories (5 KB raw, 1 KB gzip) in a small module the consent manager imports with its own lazy chunk; the purposes in cookie-list.ts for the cookie policy page and the scanner, which run on the server. Move the buyer cookie helpers to a small module that b2b.ts re-exports. Draw the theme store's parts through a lazy stand-in in components/lazy.
findings.saving: Simulated on the real chunks: 24 KB (cookie module), 12 KB (registry and common.en) and 4.8 KB (stage) leave the first scripts of the store home, the product page and Kaizena Flow's front page: 40 KB in all (store home 645 to 605 KB). A store that draws a consent banner then loads the 5 KB pattern list with the banner's script.
findings.risk: Low, if the consent manager keeps its patterns: moving the whole table away, as first written, would stop a withdrawn category's cookies from being removed.
findings.verify_note: Measured the table inside the built module (23,860 of 24,640 bytes, 6,353 gzip) and traced both other chains in the built chunks; simulated 40.4 KB. Changed: rg for KNOWN_COOKIES found the consent manager's use, so the fix must split the table, not move it whole; the saving is unchanged for pages without a banner. Not about an unused feature.

findings.title: The script budgets watch 15 of 560 routes, and the visitor's one counts a legacy file twice
findings.evidence: performance.spec.ts sums the text of every script[src] in the page; the server's HTML names the no-module polyfill (112,594 bytes, fetched by no current browser) in two tags, so 225,188 bytes of the store home's 972,000 budget are that file: the tags sum to 905,452 while the page's real first scripts are 680,264. admin-scripts.spec.ts removes repeats but still counts the polyfill once, and holds seven screens; the visitor spec holds eight routes. Outside every budget: the Work invoice at 4.27 MB, the order page at 1.95 MB, the customer and deal pages, and twelve of the thirteen lists at 1.96 MB; the thirteenth, the pages list, is inside one that was set from a measure already holding the rich text editor (2,180,000). Each build writes first-load bytes and chunk lists for all 560 routes to .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json, and nothing in the repo reads it. The admin's frame has no import rule like the storefront's: BN-1, BN-3 and BN-4 pass every check.
findings.cost: No bytes by itself; it is why 495 KB sat in the list screens and 2.9 MB in one route unnoticed, days after the last budget was set.
findings.who_pays: CI, and then every owner's browser.
findings.fix: A small script after the build that reads route-bundle-stats.json and fails on any route above its group's ceiling (storefront, site, admin screen, editor, builder), printing the worst five. Count distinct files without no-module scripts in both specs. Walk imports from the admin frame's client roots and fail on zod, @supabase, lib/i18n, lib/admin-text and any catalogue value import.
findings.saving: Keeps what the other findings save. Budgets after the cuts are in the metrics.
findings.risk: Low. The ceilings need one honest measure after the cuts. The stats file is written by Next's build code and is not in its docs, so a Next upgrade may change its shape; the script should fail loudly when the file or its fields are missing.
findings.already_tracked: Partly: PERF-11 (done) set the per-route budgets; code review step 3.4 (Open) asks for the page editor in the budgets (it is there since 31 October); a check over all routes is not planned.
findings.verify_note: Re-read both specs and recomputed the store home's count from the saved HTML (19 tags, 18 distinct, the polyfill twice: 905,452 against 680,264). Confirmed nothing outside the first draft's own files reads the stats file. Changed: 15 routes, not 14; one of the thirteen lists is inside a budget; the stats file is an undocumented output.

findings.title: One stylesheet for shoppers and owners: a quarter of what a shopper downloads styles only the admin
findings.evidence: globals.css is imported by every root layout and scans all of src, so one file (3-w0shgm-eqtf.css, 183,124 bytes raw, 32.0 KB gzip) serves every page. Its utilities layer is 115 KB. By where each class name is written, 770 utility rules (45.6 KB) appear only under components/admin, app/admin or lib/admin-*, 31.8 KB only elsewhere and 31.0 KB in both (the auditor: 54.6, 26 and 27, counting nested rules differently). None of those admin-only classes appears in the saved HTML of the 16 public pages measured. Rebuilt without them the file is 136.0 KB raw and 25.3 KB gzip. The browser's coverage figure (20 to 31% unused) is not a measure of this: it is the same on the admin home (31%) as on a store home (30%), and by class names a store home's HTML uses 177 of 1,831 utility rules, 10 KB of 113. One global sheet of single-purpose classes is how Tailwind works; what can be cut is the other audience's share.
findings.cost: 6.8 to 8.0 KB gzip (47 to 56 KB raw) of render-blocking CSS on a shopper's first page of each store; small beside the scripts.
findings.who_pays: A shopper's browser, first page per store; the admin pays the mirror image (about 32 KB raw of public-only utilities), which matters less.
findings.fix: A second Tailwind entry for the public layouts whose @source leaves out components/admin, app/admin and lib/admin-*; the admin keeps the full one, since the builder previews store parts. Class names that only the builder's option lists write but stores draw must live in shared lib files or an inline source list; a test can render the themes and compare.
findings.saving: Measured by rebuilding the file: 183.1 to 136.0 KB raw, 32.0 to 25.3 KB gzip for every public page (the auditor's rebuild: 127.3 and 24.0).
findings.risk: Medium to high for a small gain. A second Tailwind scan adds build memory, and docs/build-memory.md says the Vercel build has about 0.8 GB of margin and was killed once on 11 November. A class written only in admin code but drawn on a store would lose its style. Do it last, after the build has room.
findings.already_tracked: no. docs/build-memory.md explains the present @source lines (memory), which a second entry must respect.
findings.verify_note: Split the built file myself by layer and rule and looked each class up by folder: admin-only 45.6 KB against the auditor's 54.6, rebuilt gzip 25.3 against 24.0. Refuted one line of evidence: the coverage share is not 'that share'; coverage undercounts, and the admin home shows the same 31%. Added a direct check: no admin-only class is in any saved public page. The saving is real but among the smallest here.

findings.title: 40% of the built client JavaScript is second copies of modules; a browser meets about 14% of it while moving around
findings.evidence: Split by Turbopack's module ids, 550 of the 1,079 modules in .next/static/chunks sit in more than one file, and the extra copies are 7,222,830 bytes (6.89 MB) of 17.1 MB. The feature registry (5.5 KB) is in 90 files, blocks.en (53 KB) in 7, platform.en (43 KB) in 5, a 13 KB export table in 12, the cookie table in 6. Next's docs say this is the chunker's trade: merging chunks helps a first page load at the cost of moves between pages. What a browser pays is smaller than 40%: within one route's own first-load list 7.5 KB is loaded twice (the auditor's 16 to 110 KB per page counted other routes' chunks fetched by prefetch); visiting all 59 top-level store admin screens once downloads 3.70 MB in 96 files, of which 0.51 MB (14%) is second copies; a move from the pages list to the builder repeats 89 KB of 1,376. next.config.ts sets nothing under experimental.turbopackChunking, where Next 16.4 documents clusters and generateComponentChunks (the runtime skips what it already has).
findings.cost: About 14% of what an owner downloads while moving around the admin (measured on one tour), and 17 MB of static files per deploy of which 6.9 MB is repeats.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser while moving between admin screens; Vercel's upload on each deploy. Not a shopper's first page.
findings.fix: First the cuts above, which take the largest repeated modules out of client code (catalogues, the cookie table, the registry's catalogue import). Then, as an experiment only, build once locally with experimental.turbopackChunking (generateComponentChunks on, clusters for /admin and /s) and compare copies, per-route bytes and build memory with the same script.
findings.saving: Not measured: the option is experimental and was not built here. The repeated catalogues and tables that the other findings remove are about 1.5 MB of the 6.89 MB (sum of the largest items).
findings.risk: Medium. An experimental option on a build that is at its memory limit; measure memory with it, and expect no gain for a shopper's first page.
findings.verify_note: Reproduced the build-level numbers exactly with my own parser (1,079 modules, 550 repeated, 6.89 MB; registry in 90 files by rg). Changed the cost: the per-page 'loaded twice' figures included prefetched chunks of other routes; within a route it is 7.5 KB. Added a navigation measure (nav.mjs): 14% repeats over a tour of 59 screens. Read Next's doc: the duplication is by design and both named options exist. Lowest priority of the thirteen.
